mainTopic: Death-blood under a body, and the purity status of a woman in her days of דם טוהר
overview: This amud finishes a discussion about blood from a person who died. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה disagrees with the רבנן because he holds that blood cannot cancel blood. It then shows why he rules a crucified person's blood טהור (the death-drop stays on the wood) but a bed case טמא (blood seeps through a bed). A new משנה follows about a woman in her days of דם טוהר. At first she could only pour water for the קרבן פסח; later the חכמים ranked her as one who touched a טמא מת only for קדשים, while בית שמאי are stricter. The גמרא settles a contradiction inside that משנה by assigning its last part to אבא שאול. The next משנה lists what even בית שמאי allow her: eating מעשר, separating and naming חלה, and her saliva or blood leaving תרומה טהור. The גמרא gives the source for each of these. בית שמאי and בית הלל then argue whether she needs a second טבילה, and רב קטינא explains that the difference is about a 'long טבול יום'. Finally, a new משנה opens about a woman who saw blood on the eleventh day and immersed that evening, and it begins with בית שמאי's ruling.

steps.title: The רבנן's reason: each early drop came out separately
steps.stepSummary: The end of the רבנן's argument that the blood under the body is טהור, because the drops came out one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each first drop, and each next first drop, was separate.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of the רבנן's argument against רבי יהודה. They say the blood came out drop by drop, not in one steady stream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first drops left the body while the person was still alive, so that blood is pure. Each later drop falls into that pure blood and gets cancelled in it. So the whole puddle is considered טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: each first one, one after another (drop by drop)
separated, cut off (did not flow as one stream)
cancelling: a small amount is absorbed into a larger amount and loses its own status

phrases.english: For each first drop, one after another, is separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבנן's reasoning, which began earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood is טהור because the life-drops came first, and each later drop is cancelled into them.

steps.title: The רבנן's argument sounds strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the רבנן's argument seems very convincing, so how can רבי יהודה disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן are speaking well to רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is impressed by the רבנן's logic and challenges רבי יהודה: what could he answer to that?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first drops are pure and the later drops get cancelled, the blood should be טהור. The גמרא wants to know what reasoning lets רבי יהודה still call it טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: well, nicely, correctly
they are saying
the Sages (the majority opinion)

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה!
phrases.english: The Rabbis are saying well to Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה based on the strength of the רבנן's argument in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that the blood is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cancelling argument of the רבנן seems airtight, so רבי יהודה's position looks hard to defend.

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds blood cannot cancel blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה follows his own known view that one kind of blood cannot cancel another kind of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, because he said: blood does not cancel blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה is being consistent with a rule he holds elsewhere: blood cannot cancel blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's argument depends on the later death-drops being cancelled in the earlier pure blood. רבי יהודה does not accept that blood can cancel blood at all. So the death-blood keeps its own status, and the blood stays טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning (consistent with his view elsewhere)
blood does not cancel blood
cancels, makes something lose its status

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between the רבנן and רבי יהודה here depends on one question: can blood cancel blood? רבי יהודה says no.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
for he said: Blood does not nullify blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the disputant follows a different underlying principle (לטעמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cancelling argument should force רבי יהודה to agree the blood is טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds that blood never cancels blood, so the cancelling argument does not work for him.

steps.title: The crucified person: the death-drop stays on the wood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון says blood found under a crucified person is טמא, but רבי יהודה says טהור because the death-drop stays on the wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: a person hanging on a wooden pole, whose blood runs down to the ground, and a רביעית of blood is found under him, the blood is טמא. רבי יהודה says it is טהור, because I say the drop of death stays on the wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case: a crucified person whose blood runs down the wood. Here רבי שמעון says טמא, and רבי יהודה says טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that leaves while a person is alive is pure; blood leaving at death makes things טמא. רבי יהודה says the blood on the ground came out while he was alive, and the final death-drop is stuck on the wood. So nothing טמא reached the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: a person hanged or crucified
running down in a flow
a quarter-לוג, the amount of blood from a dead person that makes things טמא
the drop of death: the blood that leaves the body at the moment of death
rules it pure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the cases: in the bed case רבי יהודה said טמא, but here, with the wooden pole, he says טהור.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: צָלוּב עַל הָעֵץ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: One crucified on wood,
whose blood runs down to the earth,
phrases.notes: The blood is not dripping freely but running along the wood down to the ground.

phrases.english: and a quarter-log of blood is found beneath him — it is impure.
Rabbi Yehuda deems it pure,
for I say: the drop of death
remains on the wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר צָלוּב עַל הָעֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא where רבי יהודה rules the opposite way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: the blood under a crucified person is טמא. רבי יהודה: טהור, since the death-drop stays on the wood.

steps.title: Why not say the death-drop stays on the bed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה does not use the same reasoning for the person on the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, let him say for himself: I say the drop of death stays on the bed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: if the death-drop stays on the wood, why not say it stays on the bed too, and rule the bed case טהור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the bed case רבי יהודה said the blood is טמא. But his own reasoning from the crucified case seems to fit the bed just as well. So his two rulings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: let him say
for himself
bed
on top of, upon

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, let him say for himself:
phrases.notes: This refers back to the earlier case of a person lying on a bed whose blood drips down.

phrases.english: "For I say: the drop of death
remains on the bed"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's reasoning from step 4 to question his ruling in the bed case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that the bed case is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own reasoning (the death-drop stays behind) should also apply to a bed, which would make that blood טהור.

steps.title: A bed is different because blood soaks through it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a bed lets blood soak through, so the death-drop does not stay on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bed is different, because it lets things soak through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: a bed is not like a wooden pole. Blood soaks right through a bed and reaches the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a pole, the last drop can stick to the wood and never reach the ground. A bed is soft and absorbent, so the death-drop seeps through and lands with the rest of the blood. That is why רבי יהודה treats the bed case as טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: is different
lets liquid seep through, soaks through

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: on a wooden pole the death-drop stays behind (טהור), but on a bed it seeps through (טמא).

phrases.english: A bed is different, for it lets the blood seep through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling the cases apart (חילוק בין המקרים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bed should hold back the death-drop just like a wooden pole.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bed lets the blood seep through, so the death-drop reaches the floor; wood holds it back.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman in her pure-blood days poured water for the Pesach
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה starts: at first, the rule was that a woman in her days of דם טוהר could pour water for the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they used to say: a woman sitting on pure blood could pour water for the קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion ends and a new משנה begins. It tells us an earlier rule: a woman who had given birth and was in her days of דם טוהר could pour water for rinsing the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After birth and her days of impurity, a woman immerses and enters a stretch of days when blood she sees is called דם טוהר. The משנה says that at first she was allowed to pour water for the פסח. The word בראשונה signals that this was an earlier practice.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מתניתין, our משנה
at first, originally
a woman after childbirth during the days when her blood is considered pure
pours
the קרבן פסח (Pesach offering)

phrases.english: MISHNA: Initially they would say:
A woman who is sitting on the blood of purity
phrases.notes: This is a woman after childbirth who already finished her impure days and immersed.

phrases.english: would pour water for the Paschal offering.
phrases.notes: The water was used to rinse the meat of the קרבן פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At first, a woman in her days of דם טוהר was allowed to pour water for the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: The later ruling and the dispute between בית הלל and בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים changed the rule. She is like someone who touched a טמא מת, which matters only for קדשים. That is בית הלל's view. בית שמאי say she is like a טמא מת himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later they said: she is like one who touched a person made impure by a dead body, for holy things, as בית הלל say. בית שמאי say: she is even like one impure from a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rule about the woman in her days of דם טוהר. It gives the later, changed ruling and the argument between בית הלל and בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first she could only pour the water from a vessel, not touch it. Now the חכמים rank her as 'one who touched a טמא מת' only for real קדשים, so she may even touch the פסח water. בית שמאי are stricter and compare her to the טמא מת himself.

keyTerms.meaning: They changed their ruling and said
Someone who touched a person made impure by a dead body
Holy items, like קרבנות
A person made impure by contact with a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'one who TOUCHED a טמא מת' (a lower level) with 'a טמא מת' himself (a higher level). This difference is exactly what בית הלל and בית שמאי argue about.

phrases.english: They then said:
phrases.notes: This continues the משנה from step 7. The old rule was that she may pour; now the חכמים change it.

phrases.english: She is like one who touched a person impure from a corpse
with regard to holy items,
according to the words of בית הלל.
בית שמאי say:
She is even like one impure from a corpse.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת לְקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 7 by giving the revised ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per בית הלל, she is like one who touched a טמא מת with regard to קדשים. Per בית שמאי, she is like a טמא מת.

steps.title: Inference from the first part: pour yes, touch no
steps.stepSummary: The משנה let her pour but not touch the water. That shows חולין kept at קודש-level purity are treated like קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Pouring, yes. Touching, no. So חולין made with the purity of קודש are like קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by reading the first part of the משנה closely and pulling out a general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water for rinsing the פסח is really חולין, but it was kept with קודש-level care. Since she may not touch it, the water must be treated as strictly as real קודש. So the principle is that חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש count like קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: She pours (from a vessel)
She touches
Apparently / this shows that
Non-holy food or drink prepared with the purity standards of holy items

phrases.english: GEMARA
Pouring, yes,
phrases.notes: This refers back to step 7, where she was allowed to pour the water for the פסח.

phrases.english: touching, no.
Apparently, non-sacred items
that were prepared with the purity of holy items
are like holy items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by drawing a principle from the רישא of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש are treated like קודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the משנה: she may pour the פסח water but may not touch it.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה seems to say the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says her strictness applies 'to קדשים.' That suggests it does not apply to חולין, so חולין at קודש-level purity are NOT like קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last part: 'like one who touched a טמא מת for קדשים.' For קדשים, yes. For חולין, no. So חולין made with the purity of קודש are not like קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 9 by reading the last part of the same משנה, which seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לקדשים' limits her strictness to real holy items. The פסח water is חולין, so she should be allowed to touch it. That contradicts the רישא, which forbade touching.

keyTerms.meaning: Now say (look at) the last part of the משנה
Non-holy, ordinary items
Are not like holy items

steps.confusionAlert: Both inferences come from the same משנה. The problem is that the רישא and סיפא seem to contradict each other; nothing outside the משנה is involved.

phrases.english: Say the last part:
They then said

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת לְקָדָשִׁים —
phrases.english: she is like one who touched a corpse-impure person, for holy items —
for holy items, yes,
for non-sacred items, no,
apparently, non-sacred items prepared
with the purity of holy items
are not like holy items!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 9 using the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle from the רישא that חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש are like קודש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא limits the strictness to קדשים, which implies חולין at קודש-level purity are not like קודש. This creates an internal contradiction in the משנה.

steps.title: The last part follows אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the סיפא follows אבא שאול. He holds that a טבול יום counts as a ראשון for קודש: he makes two items טמא and disqualifies a third.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is the משנה? It is אבא שאול. A ברייתא teaches that אבא שאול says: a טבול יום is first-level for קודש, so he makes two items impure and disqualifies one more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by naming a specific תנא for the last part of the משנה and quoting a ברייתא with his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול gives a טבול יום the stronger status of a ראשון only for real קודש. For anything else, including חולין kept at קודש-level purity, he stays at the weaker level and does not make them טמא. That is exactly the סיפא's 'לקדשים, yes; לחולין, no', so the סיפא follows אבא שאול, while the רישא follows the view that such חולין are like קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is our משנה?
Someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall to become fully טהור
First-level impurity (a ראשון)
To make two items impure and disqualify a third

steps.whatToRemember: The רישא suggests that חולין kept at קודש-level purity are like קודש. The סיפא is explained as following אבא שאול, who ranks a טבול יום as a ראשון for קודש.

phrases.english: Whose view is the משנה?
It is אבא שאול,
as it is taught: אבא שאול says:
one who immersed today is first-level for holy items,
to make two impure
phrases.notes: The first item he touches becomes second-level and passes impurity to a next item, which becomes third-level.

phrases.english: and to disqualify one.
phrases.notes: A third item becomes fourth-level. It is unfit to eat but does not pass impurity on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the סיפא to a specific תנא (אבא שאול)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה follows one view, so the רישא and סיפא contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא follows אבא שאול, who treats a טבול יום as a ראשון for real קודש. Its limit 'לקדשים' therefore reflects his view.

steps.title: Both sides agree she may eat מעשר and separate חלה
steps.stepSummary: Even בית שמאי agree that a woman in her days of דם טוהר may eat מעשר שני, and may separate חלה from her dough and name it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: And they agree that she may eat מעשר. She may also separate חלה from her dough, bring it near the dough, and call it by the name חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists things that even בית שמאי, the stricter side, agree this woman is allowed to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 8, בית שמאי treated her very strictly, like a טמא מת himself. Here the משנה shows the limit of that strictness: for מעשר שני and for separating חלה, both sides agree she is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree. Here the stricter side, בית שמאי, agrees with בית הלל.
Here this means מעשר שני, the second tithe, which is eaten in ירושלים in purity.
The portion of dough that must be given to a כהן.
Brings near. She brings the separated חלה close to the rest of the dough.
Calls it by name. She announces that this piece is חלה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And they agree that she eats second tithe
phrases.notes: "They" means בית שמאי. Even they agree with בית הלל on these points.

phrases.english: and she separates חלה from her dough
and she brings it near and calls it by its name

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from steps 7-8 by listing what בית שמאי agree to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree that a woman in her days of טוהר may eat מעשר שני and may separate and name חלה.

steps.title: Her saliva or blood of purity does not make תרומה טמא
steps.stepSummary: Both sides also agree that if her saliva or her blood of purity falls on a loaf of תרומה, the loaf stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if some of her saliva or her blood of purity fell on a loaf of תרומה, both sides agree that the loaf is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another point that even בית שמאי agree to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think her strict status would also make her body fluids טמא. The משנה says no: even with תרומה, her saliva and her דם טוהר do not make the loaf טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Saliva.
Blood seen during the days of purity after birth. It does not make her טמא.
A loaf of תרומה, food that belongs to a כהן and must be kept טהור.

phrases.english: And if some of her saliva fell
or some of her blood of purity
onto a loaf of תרומה
they agree that it is pure

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נָפַל מֵרוּקָּהּ וּמִדַּם טׇהֳרָהּ עַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third point that בית שמאי agree to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her saliva and her blood of purity do not make תרומה טמא, according to both sides.

steps.title: Does she need another טבילה when her days of purity end?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say she must go to the מקוה again at the end of her days of purity. בית הלל say she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say she needs a טבילה at the end. בית הלל say she does not need a טבילה at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new argument: when her days of purity are over, does she need a second טבילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: She already went to the מקוה when her days of טומאה ended. בית שמאי say that טבילה is not enough, and she needs another one before eating תרומה or קדשים. בית הלל say the first טבילה already counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A טבילה at the end, meaning when the days of purity are finished.

steps.confusionAlert: "At the end" does not mean the end of her days of טומאה. Everyone agrees she goes to the מקוה then. The argument is only about a second טבילה when the days of purity are over.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
she needs immersion at the end
And Beit Hillel say:
she does not need immersion at the end

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי agree to the easier rules (מעשר, חלה, her saliva and blood on תרומה), but they argue about needing a second טבילה at the end.
steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים צְרִיכָה טְבִילָה בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from points they agree on to a new argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי require a second טבילה when her days of purity end. בית הלל do not.

steps.title: Source for why she may eat מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first rule of the משנה: right after going to the מקוה, a person may eat מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This is as מר said: once he has gone to the מקוה and come up, he may eat מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by giving the source for the משנה's first rule, that she may eat מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who went to the מקוה today has to wait until nightfall for תרומה and קדשים. For מעשר שני, though, he may eat right away. This woman has already gone to the מקוה, so even בית שמאי agree she may eat מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: He went into the מקוה and came up.
Someone who went to the מקוה today and is waiting for nightfall to become fully טהור.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
As the Master said:
he immersed and came up
he may eat second tithe

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why בית שמאי agree here: מעשר is less strict than תרומה and קדשים, so a טבילה earlier that day is enough.
steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר טָבַל וְעָלָה אוֹכֵל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first rule of the משנה (step 12) and gives its source.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that even בית שמאי let her eat מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Master's teaching that someone who went to the מקוה today may eat מעשר right away.

steps.title: Why she may separate חלה from her dough
steps.stepSummary: Dough that still needs חלה taken from it is not treated like חלה itself, so her touching it causes no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says she may separate חלה. The reason is that ordinary dough that has not yet had חלה taken from it is not treated like חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's rule that this woman may separate חלה from her dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman in her days of purity is treated like a טבול יום, who can disqualify holy food. Here she is touching dough that still needs חלה separated from it. That dough is still חולין, not חלה, so her touch does not disqualify it.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates, cuts off a piece
The portion of dough given to the כהן
Ordinary, non-holy food
Still needing חלה separated from it (טבל for חלה)

phrases.english: And she separates her חלה.
Ordinary food that still needs חלה taken from it
is not considered like חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה's rules, moving on to the חלה rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough that still needs חלה separated from it is not treated like חלה, so she may handle it.

steps.title: Why she brings the separated piece close to the dough
steps.stepSummary: She keeps the separated piece near the rest of the dough because it is a מצוה to separate from produce that is close by.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says she brings it near. This is because the Master said: it is a מצוה to separate תרומה from produce that is right next to the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the משנה's detail that she brings the separated piece close to the rest of the dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This detail is not about טומאה at all. It follows a general rule that the gift should be separated while it is next to the produce it covers. So she follows the normal way of doing the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings it near, keeps it next to
To separate תרומה (or a similar gift)
Produce that is next to the rest

phrases.english: And she brings it near.
As the Master said:
It is a מצוה to separate from what is nearby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the next detail of the same חלה rule.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's detail that she brings the separated piece near the dough
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that it is a מצוה to separate from produce that is nearby

steps.title: Why the משנה needs to say she may name it חלה
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the חכמים would make a decree against naming it, in case she touches it. The משנה teaches that there is no such decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says she gives it the name חלה. You might have thought: let us decree against this, in case she comes to touch it from the outside. So the משנה teaches us that she may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to say she may name it חלה. Without it, we might have guessed the חכמים forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she names it, the piece becomes real חלה, which her touch could disqualify. We might have expected a גזירה forbidding her from naming it, in case she touches it. The משנה tells us there is no such גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Names it, declares it to be חלה
You might have thought
Let us make a rabbinic decree (גזירה)
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: And she gives it a name.
It would enter your mind to say:
Let us decree, in case
she comes to touch it from the outside?
So it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: The משנה spells out that she may name it, so we know there is no decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the חלה rule by addressing why naming it needed to be said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She may name the piece חלה, and there is no decree out of concern that she will touch it.

steps.title: Why her saliva does not make the תרומה טמא
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that liquids coming out of a טבול יום do not pass on טומאה, except a זב's liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that if her saliva falls on תרומה, the תרומה stays טהור. As we learned: liquids that come out of a טבול יום are like liquids he touches, and neither makes things טמא. The exception is liquids of a זב, who is an אב הטומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the rule that her saliva or blood of purity does not make a loaf of תרומה טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is like a טבול יום, and a משנה rules that his body's liquids are like liquids he touches. Neither one passes on טומאה. The only exception is a זב, whose own liquids are an אב הטומאה, and she is not a זב.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquid
Someone who went to the מקוה today but must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור
A man with an impure discharge
A primary source of טומאה
Make things טמא

steps.whatToRemember: A woman in her days of purity is like a טבול יום. She may handle חלה dough and name it, and her saliva or blood does not make תרומה טמא, because a טבול יום's liquids do not pass on טומאה.

phrases.english: And if some of her saliva fell.
As we learned in a משנה:
The liquids of a טבול יום,
meaning the liquids that come out of him,
are like the liquid that he touches,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "like liquid."

phrases.english: and both of these do not make things טמא,
except for the liquids of a זב,
which are a primary source of טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the משנה's rule about saliva falling on תרומה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that her saliva or blood of purity leaves a loaf of תרומה טהור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in טבול יום: liquids coming from a טבול יום do not pass on טומאה, except those of a זב

steps.title: What is the difference between בית שמאי and בית הלל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית שמאי's view in the משנה and asks what practical difference there is between them and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the words 'בית שמאי' in the משנה: what is the practical difference between them and בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points back to בית שמאי's opinion in the משנה. It asks what the real-life difference is between their view and בית הלל's view. This question sets up רב קטינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say a יולדת needs another immersion at the end of her days of טהרה. בית הלל say the immersion at the end of her days of טומאה is enough. The גמרא wants to know what practical point depends on this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (What practical result depends on their argument?)
A woman who has given birth

phrases.english: Beit Shammai.
phrases.notes: These words point back to בית שמאי's view in the משנה: she needs another immersion at the end of her days of טהרה.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the dispute in the משנה after explaining the points both sides agree on (מעשר, חלה, and her saliva on תרומה).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical point of disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the second immersion.

steps.title: רב קטינא: the difference is a 'long טבול יום'
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא answers that the difference between them is whether she counts as a 'long טבול יום' during her days of טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: the difference between them is a 'long טבול יום'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא gives the answer. The two opinions differ on whether this woman counts as a 'long טבול יום'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום is someone who has already immersed but is not yet fully pure. This woman is in that in-between status for the whole long stretch of her days of טהרה. בית שמאי say that after so long she cannot rely on her earlier immersion and must immerse again. בית הלל say the earlier immersion still works when her days end.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who has immersed but is not yet fully pure
A 'long טבול יום': someone in that in-between status for a long time
There is (a difference) between them

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about whether a יולדת is a 'long טבול יום' during her days of טהרה, which decides whether she needs a second immersion.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
A 'long tevul yom' is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means someone who immersed and stays in the in-between status for a long stretch, here the whole time of her days of טהרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: טְבוּל יוֹם אָרוֹךְ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is whether she counts as a 'long טבול יום' during her days of טהרה.

steps.title: New משנה: she sees blood on the eleventh day and immerses that evening
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes a woman who sees blood on the eleventh day, immerses that evening, and is with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who sees blood on the eleventh day, immerses that evening, and is with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins by describing the case. The rulings come in the next step, so this line sets up the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eleventh day is the last of the eleven days in which bleeding can make a woman a זבה. After one day of blood she must wait one clean day, called שומרת יום כנגד יום. Here she did not wait. She immersed that same evening and was with her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The eleventh day, the last of the days in which she can become a זבה
A woman who must wait one clean day for each day she saw blood
She was with her husband

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman who sees blood on the eleventh day,
phrases.notes: This is the last of the eleven days when bleeding can make her a זבה.

phrases.english: and she immersed in the evening, and was with her husband —
phrases.notes: She immersed that same evening, without first waiting one clean day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a woman who saw blood on the eleventh day and immersed that same evening without waiting a clean day.

steps.title: בית שמאי: they pass on טומאה and must bring a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי rule that the woman and her husband pass on טומאה to what they lie or sit on, and both must bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: they make משכב and מושב טמא, and they are obligated to bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives בית שמאי's ruling on the case. The woman and her husband both pass on טומאה to things they lie or sit on, and both must bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she did not wait her one clean day, בית שמאי treat her as still a זבה, and her immersion does not help. That gives her husband the טומאה of a זב too, so both of them make משכב and מושב טמא. Both also need a קרבן for the relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: Things meant for lying or sitting on, which become טמא from a זב or זבה
They make (things) טמא
They are obligated to bring a קרבן
A woman with an unusual flow of blood, who has a strong level of טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: The plural words 'מטמאין' and 'חייבין' cover both the woman and her husband, not only her.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
they make items for lying and sitting impure,
phrases.notes: 'They' means both her and her husband. Without her clean day she still counts as a זבה.

phrases.english: and they are obligated to bring an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר: מְטַמְּאִין מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's ruling on the case set up in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the woman and her husband both make משכב and מושב טמא and both must bring a קרבן.
